gaps.explanation: The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unusual. An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: Don't ___ your children — let them make their own mistakes (PROTECT).
gaps.hint: protect too much (over-); a base verb is needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means excessively: overprotect means to protect too much. A base verb follows 'Don't'.
'Beyond recognition' is the fixed phrase; after 'beyond' a noun is needed.
After 'complete' a noun is needed: darkness (-ness noun of 'dark').
A bank manager is a person; 'management' is the activity and 'manage' is the verb.

gaps.sentence: She was praised for her ___ (TOLERATE) of other viewpoints.
The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.

gaps.sentence: After the fire, the theatre had to be completely ___ (BUILD).
gaps.hint: build again after destruction (re-); past participle needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: rebuilt. The passive needs the past participle after 'had to be'.
